posts.text:
A vegan has brought his dog to the vet, and the dog has been building a case.

Owner: "He's plant-based. Two years now. He's thriving."

Vet: "He's eating the corner of my desk."

Owner: "He's curious."

Vet: "What does he get at home?"

Owner: "Sweet potato, lentils, brown rice, a pea protein kibble and a supplement powder. Taurine, carnitine, B12, the lot. It's nutritionally complete."

Vet: "What's in the powder?"

Owner: "Everything he'd be missing."

Vet: "So the diet's complete once you add the things that aren't in it."

Owner: "That's how all diets work."

Vet: "It isn't how a rabbit works. Has he been stealing?"

Owner: "Stealing?"

Vet: "It says here he's been in three times this year. A pound of sausages off a neighbour's barbecue. The cat's dinner, daily, until you moved the bowl. And in March, a pigeon."

Owner: "He found the pigeon."

Vet: "He found it in the air?"

Owner: "It was already compromised."

Vet: "By what?"

Owner: "By him."

Vet: "And the cat. How's the cat?"

Owner: "The cat's vegan as well."

Vet: "The cat's a pound heavier than at Christmas and next door have lost eleven goldfish."

Owner: "You can't prove that."

Vet: "I'm not the one she's leaving the heads for."

Owner: "Look. I'm not here for a lecture. He's got loose stools, he's shedding, and he stares at me while I eat. I want to know what's wrong with him."

Vet: "Nothing's wrong with him. He's a dog. Forty-two teeth, most of them built for cutting. A gut that's done with dinner before yours has finished the starter. He's descended from an animal that follows deer through snow for a week. You've handed him a casserole."

Owner: "Dogs are omnivores. Everyone knows that."

Vet: "Dogs are opportunists. He'll eat a sock. That's not a food group."

Owner: "The packet has a wolf on it."

Vet: "The packet's lying. The wolf isn't."

Owner: "He chose this. I put down a bowl of the kibble and a bowl of chicken once, to give him the choice."

Vet: "And?"

Owner: "It wasn't a controlled test."

Vet: "Which did he eat?"

Owner: "He ate the chicken, then the bowl the chicken was in, then he guarded the fridge."

Vet: "I'll put that down as a preference."

Owner: "It's my values. He lives in my house."

Vet: "He does. And every living thing in your house has been lied to about lunch except him. He knows exactly what he is. He's just waiting for you to go out."

Owner: "So what do you recommend?"

Vet: "Meat."

Owner: "Is there a plant-based version of that advice?"

Vet: "Yes. Feed the lentils to a chicken. Then stand well back."

posts.text:
The Council of the EU has imposed new sanctions on 12 individuals and 101 entities involved in financing Russia's war and supporting its shadow fleet.

The list includes nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, the sole shareholder of Russian retail giant Wildberries, and an individual controlling the majority stake in another major Russian e-commerce company, Ozon.

The sanctions also target entities and businesspersons in the Russian oil and energy sector. The energy companies listed today manage Russian refineries and the St. Petersburg oil terminal and are active in the exploration and production segment.

Companies from the UAE, China, Seychelles and Oman that buy Russian oil have also been sanctioned, along with businesspeople linked to vessels that illegally transport Russian oil and engage in high-risk shipping activities.

Those sanctioned are subject to an asset freeze, and it is prohibited to provide them with funds or economic resources either directly or indirectly or for their benefit. Also, a travel ban to the EU applies to the listed individuals.

Separately, the Council sanctioned 30 individuals and two entities involved in Russian disinformation campaigns and cyberattacks.

Years ago, Elon Musk predicted:

“Solar electricity will become by far the biggest source of power for civilization”

Today, we're watching that vision become reality

In 2015, solar generated just 256 TWh of electricity globally

A decade later, annual solar generation has surpassed 2,700 TWh

That's more than a 10X increase in just ten years

Solar also accounted for 83% of the growth in global electricity demand during the first half of 2025

And renewables have now overtaken coal in global electricity generation

What Elon Musk envisioned years ago is unfolding right in front of us

The Sun is a gigantic fusion reactor in space, delivering more energy to Earth in a single hour than humanity consumes in an entire year

We're still capturing only a tiny fraction of it

Solar generation is accelerating, battery storage is expanding, and the world is moving toward a future of abundant, sustainable energy

And this transformation is only getting started

posts.text:
In 2014, NASA awarded Boeing $4.2 BILLION to develop Starliner

SpaceX received just $2.6 BILLION for Crew Dragon

Now look at the results:

• Boeing Starliner: Just one crewed flight and got two astronauts stuck on the ISS for over 9 months in space before SpaceX sent Dragon to rescue them

• SpaceX Crew Dragon: 21 crewed missions since 2020, carrying astronauts to orbit for NASA and private customers, saving NASA billions of dollars

Boeing received $1.6 BILLION more in the original NASA contract

Yet SpaceX ended up bringing Boeing's own astronauts back to Earth

Introduction: Governance as a Public Trust 

Peter Obi

When I took office as Governor of Anambra State, our beloved state was at a critical juncture.  Leadership had become increasingly disconnected from the people, and many of the essential institutions needed to support a modern society were weak, ineffective, or absent altogether. We understood that governance could not continue according to established habits. It needed to be reconceived as a solemn public trust founded on transparency, prudence, accountability, and demonstrable results.

Our governing philosophy rested on four principles: character, competence, capacity, and compassion. We understood that leadership was not a platform for self-promotion, political slogans, or the pursuit of personal acclaim. Its purpose was to improve the circumstances of ordinary citizens. It meant converting public resources into concrete benefits and ensuring that government’s foremost responsibility was to serve the people. Achieving this demanded more than good intentions; it required a clear vision, careful planning, and disciplined execution.

Among our earliest findings was that the state lacked a unified development plan to direct its priorities and determine how resources should be allocated. We therefore promptly created the Ministry of Economic Planning to establish the institutional foundation for deliberate, coordinated, and sustainable development. After completing the necessary groundwork and consultations, we launched the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy (ANIDS).

At that time, the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) were being pursued worldwide across eight clearly defined priorities: eliminating extreme poverty and hunger; achieving universal primary education; advancing gender equality and empowering women; reducing child mortality; improving maternal health; combating HIV/AIDS, malaria and other diseases; promoting environmental sustainability; and fostering a global partnership for development.

We adopted ANIDS as our overarching development philosophy and strategic framework for advancing these objectives, tailoring them to the distinctive circumstances, needs and development priorities of Anambra State. Instead of viewing the MDGs as remote international benchmarks, we worked to convert their aims into practical policies, programs and measurable results that would produce tangible improvements in the lives of our people.

We also undertook a deliberate effort to redefine the state’s identity, changing its public image from ‘Home for All’ to ‘The Light of the Nation’. This was not merely a change in slogan; it reflected our resolve to restore public confidence in government, renew civic pride and show that Anambra could serve as a model of purposeful leadership and development.

The ANIDS Blueprint: A Comprehensive Framework for Development

ANIDS served as the foundation for our commitment to broad-based and balanced development. We did not accept the idea that government could focus on a single sector while leaving others behind. We recognized that education, healthcare, infrastructure, security, agriculture and capable public institutions were mutually dependent. Advancement in one area could not be sustained without commensurate progress elsewhere. Accordingly, we pursued development across every sector, guided by defined priorities, disciplined planning and prudent stewardship of public resources.

Central to this vision was the restoration of the dignity of the Anambra person. We understood that dignity could not be restored through rhetoric alone. It was evident in the condition of roads and other infrastructure, the availability of healthcare, the quality of education, the performance of public institutions and the way government treated its workers, pensioners and traditional institutions.
